asks.text: To go live, the hero collection has to move into the real game save and its backups. That's a save change, with an update in save-storage.js's UPDATES list and in save-backups.html. It would hold: fragments per hero, chests opened, the equipped hero, when each chest comes back, the Hero Crests balance, the last chest and purchase receipts, and an unseen result. Until Noah OKs it, the…
This run had no browser. On the test site at 320×610, 375×812, 390×844 and 430×932, from a new save (reset page), tap the fourth tab (Heroes). Check that:
Open chest 6 (Dev tools can add opened chests). Check that the UNCOMMON HEROES UNLOCKED line fits at all four sizes.

Tap a found hero with enough Crests, then Buy 1 fragment, and Buy 2 to unlock. Check that the Confirm line and its buttons fit at all four sizes. Then equip another unlocked hero and check that TAP on Quest changes.

Timings, inside your ranges: lid 0.38s, orb rising 0.38s, chest shrinking 0.26s, then the strip slides (up to about 1s) and the orb flies for 0.78s. The landing sparkle lasts about 1s. A whole opening takes about 2½ seconds. I think that's right for three chests a day. If it feels slow, the flight is the easiest part to shorten.
A used chest still opens the chest screen, so you can look at the odds at any time. OPEN is greyed out there, so a used chest can never be opened by mistake.
The odds are one list of all ten rarities, one line each: colour, name, Chest N if it isn't open yet, and the chance. The old 5-column table overflowed on small phones, and this list doesn't.
To keep the screen light, some things moved. Each rarity's fragment price is in that hero's details, and the Crests each rarity gives are under ?. The chest screen shows only the odds.
Cards on unlocked heroes show the count toward the next mastery rank (3/8, 8/14), so you can see progress at a glance without opening the details.

The shelf, chests, orb and sparkles are drawn in code, in the same navy and old gold as the rest of Heroes. If you'd like hand-made shelf and chest art later, I'd suggest a separate art batch in the Artwork Inbox once you've tried this.
If you switch apps in the middle, the result is already saved. When you come back, it plays a short landing on the hero instead of the whole chest animation.
Everything on Heroes is still a test-site preview, kept on the device and outside your save. On the real game the tab only says "Coming Soon".

The advised Party DPS is the boss's HP divided by 30 seconds, plus 10%, rounded up (747 HP gives 28). It leaves out tapping, so a player who taps can win below the number. I think that's the right way round for a suggestion.

asks.text: Do you want a quicker start (note 2)? I suggest B: the first House costs 12 Wood · 6 Stone and the first Farm 10 Wood · 3 Stone, and nothing else changes. Or keep it as it is.

#144 replaces Haven's land rings with patches you clear one at a time. That needs a new version of Haven's own test save (v5 → v6). Joshua says his test town can be started over. I suggest OK, test site only: a fresh start under a new key, with the v5 save kept untouched as a backup. The real game's saves aren't touched. #145's fuller resource layout is built on that new map, so it waits on…

Build #144 and #145's resource layout together once Noah OKs the v6 Haven test save. That means the raised home clearing, patches with Clear and lock badges, a short Land window with Find Next Clearing, and the palisade and raids following the new edge. It also means clustered trees and rocks, about 20–30% more in the outer patches, and a clear middle. Then check that each early patch has…

Take phone pictures on the test site at 320×610, 375×812, 390×844 and 430×932, starting from a new save (? → Reset demo, then Start). Get the suggestion box with Find and the gold pointer after tapping it, chips mid-hit on a tree and a stone, a stone crumbling, and a tap on a tree at the smallest zoom. Also get the Farm's bar with − / + (0 / 2, then 1 / 2), "No free workers" with Reassign in…

Is the start drawn out? Yes, a bit. I measured it with the hits and prices you have now. Swinging as fast as Haven allows (about 2 a second), the first House takes 114–134 hits (about 1 minute) and the Farm 176–222 hits in total (about 1½–2 minutes). Tapping once a second, it's about 1½–2 minutes to the House and 2½–4 minutes to the Farm. The lower numbers are with your first settler on Auto…

If you want a quicker start, here are two options. A: Pines give 3 Wood instead of 2, and berry bushes 2 Wood instead of 1. The first House would take about 90 hits, and everything later would get a bit quicker too. B: Only the first House and Farm get cheaper: House 12 Wood · 6 Stone, Farm 10 Wood · 3 Stone. The first House would take about 70 hits, and nothing later would change. I'd pick B,…

Find points at what you're shortest of, counted in hits. For the first House that's Wood (20 Wood takes more hits than 8 Stone). Once you have the Wood, it points at Stone. I think that's the most useful thing to point at.
Find prefers pines and oaks over bushes for Wood, because they give more per hit. It also prefers nodes your workers can walk up to.

Each discovered companion pays 1 Lore Shard, once. These amounts were Codex's suggestion, not yours. That's 30 Shards for the current 30 companions, less than one Shard per summon. I think it's fine as a small thank-you. Raise it if you want discoveries to feel like a real reward.

Completing a rarity pays a one-time 10 Lore Shards (Common, Uncommon and Rare today, 30 in all). Rare has only 4 companions but pays the same as Common's 16. I'd try paying more for rarer tiers, for example Common 10, Uncommon 15, Rare 25.
Companions you released still count, because the game remembers every species you've discovered. Long-time players will see one bigger claim the first time.

A rarity that later gets new companions keeps the bonus it already paid. Each new companion still pays its own Shard. If the rarity grows before you've claimed its bonus, you need the new companions too.
Codex also asked for "claimed" on every card. I used one small line under each card ("+1 Shard ready" or "Shard claimed"). If it feels busy, I can show only "ready".

items.title: Rescue prologue and starter selection

asks.text: After the next test-site build, check that test-build.json on https://lorebound-dev.github.io/ includes #161 at 7baaf1e. If it's left out for a clash, bring it up to date with main.

The meteor slide now lasts 1.5 seconds instead of 3.4, and the meteor's fall and impact were sped up to fit. Fades are still 0.55 seconds. I think it reads well. If it feels rushed, 2 seconds is a safe middle.
"Then the sky broke" now uses the story's existing city picture, darkened, with a faint orange glow at the top. No new art. I like it better than plain black, and it ties the line to the meteor.

All three starters show 10 DPS before you choose. They differ only in Normal hit (19.9 / 9.9) and Crit chance (1.0% / 3.0%) for the first two. That's honest, but players may think the choice barely matters. If you want each egg to feel more different, the role line ("Thorn guardian") is the place to say more.

The tips are worded: "Tap the enemy to strike with your weapon." / "Your companions attack by themselves, even while you're away. Party DPS is their damage each second." / "Quests give rewards. Your first one is ready: open the Journal and claim it." / "Spend Lore Shards at the Rift to summon new companions. Quests and bosses give you Shards." / "Tap Gold, Party DPS or Lore Shards any time to…
The tips are remembered per phone, not in the save, so no save change was needed. A player who starts a second save on the same phone won't see them again. I think that's fine.
The tip box sits on the opposite side of the screen from what it points at. While it's open, it briefly covers part of the party row or the top buttons. It's only five taps, so I left it there.

asks.text: Ascend is being replaced by Heroes (#147). Should I drop the "what resets / what stays" list for Ascend? My suggestion: drop it if Heroes replaces Ascend. If you're keeping Ascend, I'll build it in #88.

How should we fix the Floor 1 stall? My suggestion: no number change. When a Floor 1 boss fight is lost, show "Tap the enemy to help your companions", built with the boss retry once #133 is live. The other option is Floor 1 boss health from 1,000 to 900, which fixes the three-companion starts but not the two-companion ones.
Favorite and Protect in Manage Team (area 3) need a save update, because Protect is stored per companion copy. They wait for Noah's OK on that save change. The rest of the audit doesn't wait for it.
The one-time mastery explanation (area 6, #119) only needs a save change if it's remembered per save. Remembering it on the phone needs no OK.

Look at the Auto plaque at 320×610, 375×667, 390×844 and 430×932 on the test site. From a new save: Summon, then Auto, then Start, then Stop Auto after a few summons. Check that it sits above the rail without covering the Stop button and that the text doesn't clip.

Look at the Auto setup at the same four sizes, and check that the new Reduced effects row and its 12px note fit. Turn it on, fight a few enemies, and check that damage numbers thin out and crits still show.
Post each handoff from the ledger on its owning request: #115, #118, #119, #133, #141, #142, #97, #109 and #98. Each post lists exactly what's still to build there.
Look at Save Backups at the four sizes. From a new save: Profile, then Save Backups. Check the "N/30 discovered" line.
Profile ten companions, a fight and Auto on a slowed-down browser (area 9). Check that the away popup and update popups never overlap.

The Auto plaque shows when you tap Stop and also when Auto runs out of Lore Shards, because both end the session. It hides after 12 seconds. If you'd rather it stays until you tap ×, that's a one-line change.
Reduced effects allows two damage numbers on screen at once, and always lets a critical hit through. I think two is enough to follow the fight on a small phone.

The opening is quick for most new saves. The one weak spot is the Floor 1 boss after an unlucky start. Those players need about 22 taps in the fight (about 125 with only two companions), and nothing tells them to tap.

items.quote: "Also let’s remove shardworks and replace it with a farm where you can raise pets that give bonuses to a companion. We will use the original egg mechanics but have fewer pets and new ones. So there would be a main egg that is a random rarity and take a certain amount of time to hatch. Then your hatched pets will kind of walk around around the egg in that location."

asks.text: What happens to Shardworks' Lore Shards? Right now it makes 3 to about 30 Shards an hour for players who rebuilt it. My suggestion: keep Shardworks running, reached from the Farm as it is now, until you choose a new place for those Shards. That way nobody loses what they paid for.
How much Gold does an egg cost? My suggestion: 5,000 Gold, the same as rebuilding Shardworks, so an egg a day feels like a real choice in the mid game.
What are the rarity odds? My suggestion: Common 70%, Uncommon 25%, Rare 5%, with the Commons, Uncommons and Rare equally likely within their rarity.

What are the six pets, and what does each one give the companion it's assigned to? My suggestion: 3 Common pets at +3% damage, 2 Uncommon pets at +5% critical chance or 5% faster attacks, and 1 Rare pet at +8% damage. A repeat hatch adds one bond level, up to 5, and each level adds a further 1%.
When does the Farm unlock? My suggestion: show it from the start as a quiet meadow, with eggs available after Boss 40.

Pet art. The finished game needs real art for each of the six pets: small pixel sprites with 2 to 4 walk and idle frames. Please have it made and put in your Artwork Inbox's Proposed folder, then link it in a change to this request.
Eggs and owned pets need new data in the save, added through the save update list. I won't build that until Noah OKs the save change.
Stopping Shardworks, or moving players' Shardworks upgrades to something else, changes saves that players paid Gold for. That also needs Noah's OK once Joshua decides on question 1.

Check the Farm on a phone at 320×610, 375×667, 390×844 and 430×932. From a new save, tap Farm on the bottom bar. Make sure the pets stay inside the fence and below the nest, the "Get Egg" and Shardworks buttons aren't covered, and every label is readable. Then tap Shardworks and "‹ Pet Farm" to check the way back.
Build eggs, hatching, the pet journal and assigning a pet to a companion once Joshua answers questions 1 to 5 and Noah OKs the save change.

I built only the part you can try without new decisions: the Farm screen, the nest and the wandering pets. Eggs, hatching, the pet list and companion bonuses need your numbers and new save data, which Noah has to approve. If I built them now with made-up numbers, they'd have to be redone.

The pets and the Farm icon are simple shapes drawn in code, not real art. They're only there to test the size and movement. They can't go in the real game as finished pets. The meadow is also drawn in code. If you'd like a painted background like the Shardworks mine, it would need art in your Artwork Inbox.

Pets walk only in the strip below the nest, so they never cover the egg or the buttons. With six pets that strip may feel crowded. Once the real pets exist, I'd let them walk all the way round the nest.
I agree with the request on Boss 40 for the Farm unlock instead of Shardworks' Floor 60. It gives players eggs to look forward to earlier.
It clashes with another change in progress, in home.html and navigation.js, so it isn't on the test site yet.

items.title: Rework companions: 15 per rarity, four summon bands, and brand-new Common roster
items.quote: "I want to rework all companions so far, have 4 tiers of pull chances within a rarity (abberitions are a big jump as it is currently, the other should be pretty close like within a few percentage, just for variety), have 15 per rarity, and I want al currently created companions to move up a rarity and common kept free for us to remake. Feel free to switch any around to different rarities than they are if they look cooler"

asks.text: How much stronger should each rarity be? I suggest ×1.41 per rarity: Common 10, Uncommon 14.1, Rare 20, Epic 28.3, Legendary 40, Mythic 56.6. Nobody's companion gets weaker, and none more than doubles. The other choices are today's ×2, which makes most companions 4× or 8× stronger, or keeping each companion's current damage, which makes new Commons and moved-up Uncommons hit the same.

Legendary has 14 companions, not 15. Should it open early? I suggest yes: 0.20% at Rift Level 5, rising to 1.00% at Level 46, with the 14 sharing it (Riftmourn 1.07% of Legendary). Otherwise Hollow Knight, Moonveil Stag, Stone Sentinel, Dusk Revenant and ten Realm 2 companions can't be summoned until a 15th Legendary exists.

Forgotten Watcher is the only Mythic. I suggest leaving it unsummonable until Mythic has 15 companions, as your request says. Players who own it keep it. The other choice is keeping it Legendary for now, but then Legendary would have two Aberrations.

What should a level cost for the new rarities? I suggest multipliers of Epic 5, Legendary 8 and Mythic 13, rising at the same pace as Uncommon to Rare. Without these, Epic and higher companions can't be levelled at all.
Which three new Commons should new players choose their starter from? I suggest Brackenfox, Burrbloom and Tackbolt: a Beast, a Wildgrowth and a Construct, like today's three.

The save update in the plan: it recalculates each companion's Essence so its level stays the same, moves Auto's stop choices, and adds a marker that it ran. I suggest building it last, after #119, #78, #89 and #97, and testing it on a made-up full save first.
The summon roll needs finer steps: parts per million instead of parts per 10,000. Riftmourn at Level 5 is 21 per million, which is less than one step today. That change is in ownership-v5.js.
New saves would store the starter by companion name ID (starterId), because today's starter number only reaches today's three starters. Old saves keep theirs as they are.

#78 as built keeps today's five Tome tables and adds no new rarities. So the only chance table that covers all ten rarities is #97's draft ladder, and I used it. If you change the ladder in #97, this plan follows it.

Moving companions up a rarity makes each of them rarer to summon, because each rarity is summoned less often. For example, Hollow Knight goes from about 0.5% today to about 0.02% at Level 5. That's what moving up means, but you'll notice it.

And pressing it will clear it mostly to add it to an area you can get resources and build."  "Yes and figure out if we need to render any assets or no." This is an explicit owner decision. It supports the simpler, gradual-upgrade path already sent through #140.
